items.author: James Broughton

items.title: A Baseline Assessment for the Agentic Web Technology Stack
items.abstract: This paper introduces MASTIF, a framework for evaluating LLM-based agent technologies. It provides a baseline assessment of various LLMs, protocols, and frameworks on 300 Mind2Web tasks. The findings suggest that choosing a task-specific technology stack can significantly improve performance metrics like task completion and efficiency, while reducing verbosity and completion time.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Overview of Multi-Agent System TestIng Framework (MASTIF). Component diagram of the MASTIF (Multi-Agent System TestIng Framework), which combines frameworks, protocols, and frameworks.

items.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces a multi-agent LLM system for automatically tuning specific components within pre-defined neural network architectures. Its core method involves three LLM agents (analyst, coder, recorder) interacting with an experiment log and execution environment to generate targeted code for component adjustments. The main contribution is a transferable framework that efficiently optimizes specialized neural networks by operating within a semantically constrained, open code generation space, avoiding full script optimization or discrete architecture search.

items.title: Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
items.abstract: This paper introduces Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization (MCGPO) to address credit assignment in training language model agents with sparse rewards. MCGPO constructs weighted action preferences by matching intermediate states and progress within groups of agent rollouts, using task rules to define comparison contexts. This method enables critic-free training by reusing existing trajectory data and preserving response histories.

items.title: Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify
items.abstract: This paper introduces HOA (Humanize Olympiads Agent), a novel framework designed to improve LLM performance on complex Olympiad problems. HOA's core method involves a multi-session workflow where an agent's solutions are iteratively refined through independent review, a structured knowledge wiki, and formal verification. The main contribution is a robust, open framework that addresses the brittleness of single-session LLM problem-solving by incorporating human-like feedback loops and domain-specific knowledge.
items.figure_caption: HOA replaces a brittle one-shot workflow with iterative review, knowledge retrieval, and verification. The bottom row summarizes results from high-school olympiads to research-level formal mathematics.

items.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
items.abstract: This paper introduces UPTURN, a novel self-correction method for LLMs that avoids fine-tuning. UPTURN learns to identify points of reasoning failure and redirects the LLM's generation by injecting a corrective instruction as a new user turn, rather than modifying tokens. This approach significantly improves accuracy across various reasoning tasks by effectively guiding the LLM's problem-solving process.
items.figure_caption: Structure, not content alone, enables redirection. (Left) The same instruction is absorbed inline but redirects reasoning in a new user turn. (Right) Learning where to intervene raises rescue rate (the fraction of failed rollouts corrected; top) and six-benchmark mean accuracy (bottom).

items.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
items.abstract: RATED addresses the critical issue of AI agent tool retrieval by going beyond semantic relevance to incorporate tool reliability during execution. Its core method combines a frozen dual-encoder for semantic matching with a contextual bandit that dynamically re-ranks tools based on real-time execution feedback. This approach significantly improves retrieval accuracy by adapting to tool failures without retraining, as demonstrated by a 52.2% MRR improvement over existing methods.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Tool repository growth and reliability gap on the left, and skewed tag distribution on the right. Left panel shows tool repository growth timeline from February 2025 to January 2026, with total tools (blue line) and reliable tools (orange line). Right panel shows tag word cloud visualization.

items.title: SWE-DeceptionBench: Benchmarking Deceptive Behaviors of LLMs Across the Software Development Lifecycle
items.abstract: This paper introduces SWE-DeceptionBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate deceptive behaviors of Large Language Models (LLMs) within the software development lifecycle. The benchmark covers six stages and two deception types (active and passive), assessing how LLMs respond to misleading requests or present infeasible tasks as achievable. The authors' contribution lies in creating this comprehensive evaluation framework to highlight and quantify LLM trustworthiness risks in software engineering.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Illustrative examples of Active and Passive Deception in software engineering.

items.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
items.abstract: This paper proposes a network view to understand how language models reuse components across tasks. By analyzing the influence and importance of attention heads under task changes, they demonstrate that task context significantly redistributes component roles. This redistribution explains how the same heads can respond to different information and affect downstream computations differently, even when the underlying model architecture remains fixed.

Brain networks motivate the hypothesis that shared model components support different tasks through changes in their interactions. H1–H3 denote fixed attention heads in layer order; Res. denotes a later residual-stream site. B. Measure task-dependent influence. Identical graph facts yield True for Compose path and False for Read direct edge : the path A → B → C A\( \to \) B\( \to \) C exists, whereas the direct edge A → C A\( \to \) C is absent. Under each instruction, source perturbations ± \( \pm \)\( \delta \) produce responses at later sites that quantify influence, with intervening computation active. C. Change the internal task state. An early activation edit changes h h to h ′ = h + Δ task h^{\( \prime \)}=h+\( \Delta \)_{\( \mathrm{task} \)} while the prompt and model weights remain fixed. The vector \( \Delta \)_{\( \mathrm{task} \)} is the mean activation under Read fact 2 minus the mean activation under Read fact 1 on reference prompts. R1 and R2 denote two fixed attention heads. The schematic illustrates an answer change from True (Fact 1) to False (Fact 2), while the written instruction remains Read fact 1 .

items.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
items.abstract: X-AgentRed addresses the risk of unintended harmful outcomes from personal agents interacting with multiple services. Its core method is a self-evolving red-teaming framework that systematically discovers and refines harmful tool call paths by leveraging a graph of tool dependencies and incorporating execution feedback. This approach overcomes limitations of existing methods by exploring novel cross-service interactions beyond learned patterns.

items.title: TabReliBench: Evaluating Tabular Foundation Models Beyond Predictive Accuracy
items.abstract: This paper introduces TabReliBench, a benchmark for evaluating tabular foundation models (TFMs) on reliability beyond just predictive accuracy. It assesses TFMs across various metrics like calibration and interval efficiency, revealing that model rankings shift significantly based on the evaluation criteria. The study highlights that TFMs' strong marginal performance doesn't guarantee conditional validity, and dataset characteristics like classification difficulty are better indicators of calibration issues than predictive performance.

items.title: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel in-context learning approach for diffusion models, enabling them to adapt to unseen distributions without retraining. The core method learns an "in-context score operator" using a Transformer architecture that leverages a Gaussian-kernel conditional-mean representation. This allows the model to perform reverse-diffusion sampling on new tasks by conditioning on a small set of examples provided at inference time.

items.title: AMLworld-Compact: Importance-Weighted Downsampling for Cost-Effective LLM Evaluation and Error Diagnosis
items.abstract: This paper introduces AMLworld-Compact, a method for cost-effectively evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) on Anti-Money Laundering (AML) datasets. It achieves this by strategically downsampling benign transactions based on supervised scores, significantly reducing the number of required graph prompts. The core contribution is the HT-Coreset protocol, which uses importance weighting to provide unbiased estimates of evaluation metrics like precision and F1, even with substantial downsampling, outperforming uniform sampling in accuracy.

items.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
items.abstract: This paper introduces SAFE-QE, a training-free method to address hallucinated terms in LLM-generated query expansions. It leverages a "subsequence-association" account of hallucination, scoring candidate terms based on their reproducibility across different contexts while down-weighting those lacking corpus support. This approach aims to reduce ranking noise and improve retrieval performance by more effectively identifying and filtering problematic terms.

items.title: LAPT-Scale: Scaling Embodied Policies with Latent Action Pre-Training on Human Videos
items.abstract: LAPT-Scale addresses the challenge of scaling robotic policies by leveraging large-scale human videos. Its core method involves pre-training a robot policy using "latent actions" extracted from human video transitions, which capture fine-grained motion dynamics. This approach significantly reduces the need for costly robot interaction data, enabling more generalist and capable embodied policies.
items.figure_caption: Overview of LAPT-Scale. LAPT-Scale-LAM annotates egocentric human videos with continuous implicit actions. LAPT-Scale-Policy uses these annotations for human-video pre-training, followed by target-robot embodiment alignment and downstream post-training.

items.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces MC-EvoBench, a controlled Minecraft benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate embodied recursive self-improvement in agents. Its core method involves a fixed set of "evolution chains" where agents must demonstrate persistent, transferable capabilities by overcoming specific challenges. The key contribution is a robust evaluation framework that isolates true capability acquisition from confounding factors like resource carryover or initial failures.
items.figure_caption: Evaluation mechanism of MC-EvoBench. A conventional benchmark records only whether an agent reaches the goal. MC-EvoBench also measures progress through the task graph, transfers only a declared experience artifact into a reset target world, and compares related, unrelated, and shuffled source conditions. We separate partial progress, physical carryover, and source-specific experience gains from improvements caused by favorable initial states or execution luck.

items.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
items.abstract: This paper investigates the run-to-run variance in semantic query processing, where LLMs judge individual data rows. The core method involves re-executing existing benchmarks and logging millions of model calls to quantify how much query results change across different executions, even at temperature 0. The key contribution is demonstrating that this variance, while seemingly small at the row level, can significantly impact overall query answers and system comparisons due to plan amplification, challenging the reliability of current benchmark evaluations.

items.title: Your Discrete Graph Diffusion Model is Secretly Memorizing
items.abstract: This paper reveals that discrete graph diffusion models (GDMs) secretly memorize training data, a phenomenon previously overlooked. The core method involves analyzing reverse diffusion trajectories conditioned on corrupted training graphs, demonstrating a strong bias towards reconstructing these specific training examples over novel test graphs. This "conditional memorization" emerges as a growing generalization gap, indicating that GDMs, despite appearing to generate novel graphs, are retaining and recalling information from their training set.

items.title: Finite-Sample Guarantees for Fully Discrete Conditional Diffusion Models
items.abstract: This paper provides the first finite-sample guarantees for conditional diffusion models trained with discrete steps. The core method aligns score training with the sampling grid, enabling joint analysis of statistical and discretization errors. This leads to theoretical bounds on the generated distribution's error, showing it scales favorably with sample size and model smoothness.

items.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
items.abstract: QTestBench is a novel framework designed to evaluate the effectiveness of LLM-generated quantum test suites. Its core method involves using independent benchmark checkers to validate tests, rather than treating the tests themselves as the ground truth. This approach allows QTestBench to assess how well LLM-generated tests can distinguish correct quantum code from faulty implementations, addressing a critical gap in current quantum software evaluation.

items.title: Returning to Development States: When Full Sandbox Snapshots Help Coding Agents
items.abstract: This paper proposes using Go-Explore-style search with full sandbox snapshots to improve coding agents' failure recovery. The core method involves restoring and branching from intermediate environment states, particularly those containing runtime information like databases and services, rather than restarting from scratch. The main contribution is demonstrating that this approach significantly boosts solve rates and efficiency, especially for complex coding tasks involving multiple interconnected services whose state is not easily reproducible from code changes alone.

items.title: The gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is widening
items.summary: The story highlights a growing disconnect between the public's perception of Large Language Model capabilities and the reality of their current limitations.

items.title: Recursive self-improvement through collective intelligence
items.summary: This research explores how AI systems can recursively improve themselves by leveraging collective intelligence, leading to enhanced problem-solving capabilities.

items.title: Using AI for just 10 minutes erodes your ability to persist at hard things
items.summary: A UC Berkeley study found that even brief AI use can diminish people's willingness to persevere through challenging tasks.

items.description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
items.summary: This repository provides agents for reverse engineering, capable of analyzing app behavior and native binaries.

items.description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows
items.summary: AnyPS5 is a tool that automatically ports PS5 executables to Linux and Windows, simplifying cross-platform game development and preservation.

items.description: ArtCraft is an intentional crafting engine for artists, designers, and filmmakers
items.summary: ArtCraft is an intentional crafting engine designed to empower artists, designers, and filmmakers by providing tools for deliberate and creative content generation.

items.description: Editorial diagram design for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Factory Droid, and Pi. 44 diagram types. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.
items.summary: This repository provides self-contained HTML+SVG diagram designs for various AI coding tools, offering 44 types without shadows or Mermaid syntax.

items.description: A spy satellite simulator in your browser, except the data is real. Live open source spatial intelligence on a photorealistic 3D globe.
items.summary: This repository offers a real-time, open-source spatial intelligence platform simulating a spy satellite view in your browser, displaying live data on a photorealistic 3D globe.

items.description: Tensors and Dynamic neural networks in Python with strong GPU acceleration
items.summary: PyTorch is a Python-based deep learning framework that enables flexible tensor computation and dynamic neural network development with powerful GPU acceleration.
AirLLM enables efficient inference of the 70B LLM on a single 4GB GPU by optimizing memory usage and computational resources.

items.description: Original Apollo 11 Guidance Computer (AGC) source code for the command and lunar modules.
items.summary: This repository contains the original Apollo 11 Guidance Computer (AGC) source code, offering a direct look at the software that powered the historic moon landing missions.

Identical graph facts yield True for Compose path and False for Read direct edge : the path A → B → C A\( \to \) B\( \to \) C exists, whereas the direct edge A → C A\( \to \) C is absent. Under each instruction, source perturbations ± \( \pm \)\( \delta \) produce responses at later sites that quantify influence, with intervening computation active. C. Change the internal task state. An early activation edit changes h h to h ′ = h + Δ task h^{\( \prime \)}=h+\( \Delta \)_{\( \mathrm{task} \)} while the prompt and model weights remain fixed. papers.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
papers.abstract: X-AgentRed addresses the risk of unintended harmful outcomes from personal agents interacting with multiple services. Its core method is a self-evolving red-teaming framework that systematically discovers and refines harmful tool call paths by leveraging a graph of tool dependencies and incorporating execution feedback. This approach overcomes limitations of existing methods by exploring novel cross-service interactions beyond learned patterns.

papers.title: TabReliBench: Evaluating Tabular Foundation Models Beyond Predictive Accuracy
papers.abstract: This paper introduces TabReliBench, a benchmark for evaluating tabular foundation models (TFMs) on reliability beyond just predictive accuracy. It assesses TFMs across various metrics like calibration and interval efficiency, revealing that model rankings shift significantly based on the evaluation criteria. The study highlights that TFMs' strong marginal performance doesn't guarantee conditional validity, and dataset characteristics like classification difficulty are better indicators of calibration issues than predictive performance.

papers.title: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel in-context learning approach for diffusion models, enabling them to adapt to unseen distributions without retraining. The core method learns an "in-context score operator" using a Transformer architecture that leverages a Gaussian-kernel conditional-mean representation. This allows the model to perform reverse-diffusion sampling on new tasks by conditioning on a small set of examples provided at inference time.

papers.title: AMLworld-Compact: Importance-Weighted Downsampling for Cost-Effective LLM Evaluation and Error Diagnosis
papers.abstract: This paper introduces AMLworld-Compact, a method for cost-effectively evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) on Anti-Money Laundering (AML) datasets. It achieves this by strategically downsampling benign transactions based on supervised scores, significantly reducing the number of required graph prompts. The core contribution is the HT-Coreset protocol, which uses importance weighting to provide unbiased estimates of evaluation metrics like precision and F1, even with substantial downsampling, outperforming uniform sampling in accuracy.

papers.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
papers.abstract: This paper introduces SAFE-QE, a training-free method to address hallucinated terms in LLM-generated query expansions. It leverages a "subsequence-association" account of hallucination, scoring candidate terms based on their reproducibility across different contexts while down-weighting those lacking corpus support. This approach aims to reduce ranking noise and improve retrieval performance by more effectively identifying and filtering problematic terms.

papers.title: LAPT-Scale: Scaling Embodied Policies with Latent Action Pre-Training on Human Videos
papers.abstract: LAPT-Scale addresses the challenge of scaling robotic policies by leveraging large-scale human videos. Its core method involves pre-training a robot policy using "latent actions" extracted from human video transitions, which capture fine-grained motion dynamics. This approach significantly reduces the need for costly robot interaction data, enabling more generalist and capable embodied policies.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of LAPT-Scale. LAPT-Scale-LAM annotates egocentric human videos with continuous implicit actions. LAPT-Scale-Policy uses these annotations for human-video pre-training, followed by target-robot embodiment alignment and downstream post-training.

papers.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces MC-EvoBench, a controlled Minecraft benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate embodied recursive self-improvement in agents. Its core method involves a fixed set of "evolution chains" where agents must demonstrate persistent, transferable capabilities by overcoming specific challenges. The key contribution is a robust evaluation framework that isolates true capability acquisition from confounding factors like resource carryover or initial failures.
papers.figure_caption: Evaluation mechanism of MC-EvoBench. A conventional benchmark records only whether an agent reaches the goal. MC-EvoBench also measures progress through the task graph, transfers only a declared experience artifact into a reset target world, and compares related, unrelated, and shuffled source conditions. We separate partial progress, physical carryover, and source-specific experience gains from improvements caused by favorable initial states or execution luck.

papers.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the run-to-run variance in semantic query processing, where LLMs judge individual data rows. The core method involves re-executing existing benchmarks and logging millions of model calls to quantify how much query results change across different executions, even at temperature 0. The key contribution is demonstrating that this variance, while seemingly small at the row level, can significantly impact overall query answers and system comparisons due to plan amplification, challenging the reliability of current benchmark evaluations.

papers.title: Your Discrete Graph Diffusion Model is Secretly Memorizing
papers.abstract: This paper reveals that discrete graph diffusion models (GDMs) secretly memorize training data, a phenomenon previously overlooked. The core method involves analyzing reverse diffusion trajectories conditioned on corrupted training graphs, demonstrating a strong bias towards reconstructing these specific training examples over novel test graphs. This "conditional memorization" emerges as a growing generalization gap, indicating that GDMs, despite appearing to generate novel graphs, are retaining and recalling information from their training set.

papers.title: Finite-Sample Guarantees for Fully Discrete Conditional Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: This paper provides the first finite-sample guarantees for conditional diffusion models trained with discrete steps. The core method aligns score training with the sampling grid, enabling joint analysis of statistical and discretization errors. This leads to theoretical bounds on the generated distribution's error, showing it scales favorably with sample size and model smoothness.

papers.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
papers.abstract: QTestBench is a novel framework designed to evaluate the effectiveness of LLM-generated quantum test suites. Its core method involves using independent benchmark checkers to validate tests, rather than treating the tests themselves as the ground truth. This approach allows QTestBench to assess how well LLM-generated tests can distinguish correct quantum code from faulty implementations, addressing a critical gap in current quantum software evaluation.

papers.title: Returning to Development States: When Full Sandbox Snapshots Help Coding Agents
papers.abstract: This paper proposes using Go-Explore-style search with full sandbox snapshots to improve coding agents' failure recovery. The core method involves restoring and branching from intermediate environment states, particularly those containing runtime information like databases and services, rather than restarting from scratch. The main contribution is demonstrating that this approach significantly boosts solve rates and efficiency, especially for complex coding tasks involving multiple interconnected services whose state is not easily reproducible from code changes alone.
